drag_sections.location: Paragraphs 4-7 ("Forty years of practice..." through "He had not expected the chairs to bother him, and they bothered him.")
drag_sections.why: The internal monologue and backstory on Voss's experience with dying men, while atmospheric, slows the forward movement and risks losing urgency.

standout_moments.location: Opening line: "The first thing Solomon Voss noticed, because noticing was the last profession he had left, was that August had set out four chairs."
standout_moments.why: Immediate intrigue and character voice; the four chairs are a visual and narrative hook.

standout_moments.location: "And this time," August said, "for the first time in eleven lives, I changed one thing. A small thing. The smallest thing I have ever been brave enough to change."
standout_moments.why: Major speculative reveal delivered with emotional weight and clarity, reframing the scene and raising stakes.

standout_moments.location: Final paragraph: "And Solomon Voss...tried to think of a question that August Renner could not possibly answer."
standout_moments.why: Exit leaves a direct operational question unresolved, compelling the reader to continue.

editor_notes: This chapter is a model of reader pull: the opening image is arresting, the speculative reveal lands with force, and the exit is a textbook OPENS.
The only drag is a slight overindulgence in Voss's internal diagnostics early on; consider compressing or breaking up the backstory to maintain tension.
Dialogue is crisp and character dynamics are clear without exposition.
The chapter exit is a perfect operational cliffhanger: the protagonist is challenged to ask an unanswerable question, and the reader is primed to see what happens next.
No thematic overstatement or unnecessary recap; the speculative premise is dramatized, not explained.
This is publishable-level reader experience; the only minor flag is pacing in the early interiority.

drag_sections.location: Because that was the diagnosis he had brought with him in the car, against his own discipline, on the strength of one line in the message: Bring the doctor. Not the man. The doctor. A man only wants a witness to his mind when he has begun to doubt it.

drag_sections.fix: Cut or compress; trust the reader to feel Voss's dread from the chairs and his practiced demeanor.

drag_sections.location: He had a hundred of them. Confabulation. Terminal lucidity gone grandiose. I am not dying at random; I am completing a circle. He had the name in his hand, the way you have a coin in your hand, smooth and known and the right weight.
drag_sections.why: Stacks diagnostic labels and internalizes Voss's urge to explain, after the scene has already dramatized his skepticism and unease.
drag_sections.fix: Let the coin metaphor stand; cut the explicit diagnostic stack.

standout_moments.location: August had set out four chairs. Not three and the bed. Four chairs, drawn into a loose arc around the cold hearth, and the bed pushed back against the window as if August intended to leave it behind.
standout_moments.why: The arrangement of the chairs and the bed delivers unease and foreshadows consequence through image, not explanation.

standout_moments.location: "You came here to listen to a dying man lose his mind. I'm asking you to do something harder. I'm asking you to listen to him keep it."
standout_moments.why: August's request lands as a challenge and a plea, dramatizing his clarity and the stakes without naming the emotion.

standout_moments.location: "And this time," August said, "for the first time in eleven lives, I changed one thing. A small thing. The smallest thing I have ever been brave enough to change." His gaze went, gently, to the man holding the pharmacy bag in both hands. "And because I changed it, one of you is sitting in this room who, by every other turn of this life, by all ten times before, has been dead for thirty years."
standout_moments.why: The reveal is delivered through behavior (August's gaze, Danny's reaction) and consequence, not adjectives or summary.

standout_moments.location: Voss became aware that he had not, for some seconds, taken a breath of his own. He took one now, quietly, the way you take a pulse without letting the patient feel you do it...
standout_moments.why: Physical reaction (holding breath) embodies tension and awe without naming the feeling.

standout_moments.location: And Solomon Voss... sat in the fourth chair's arc with the coin of the right diagnosis going slowly cold in his palm, and tried to think of a question that August Renner could not possibly answer.
standout_moments.why: The final image leaves the ache of uncertainty and the cost of doubt, without resolving or summarizing the theme.

editor_notes: The chapter's emotional impact is strongest when it trusts the reader to feel unease and awe through arrangement, gesture, and silence. Cut or compress the diagnostic and emotional glosses; they undercut the restraint elsewhere.
The central grief (August's dying, the cost of the change) is embodied in image and behavior—chairs, breath, gaze—rather than eulogy. Preserve this.
The ending lands with ache, not thesis: Voss's uncertainty and the unanswered question linger. Do not let later chapters explain away this ambiguity.
Hope is the weakest axis—August's act is costed, but the forward-pull is muted. Consider a sharper sense of what might be possible, even if only in subtext.
The wonder of the premise (reincarnation, altered fate) is delivered through consequence and dialogue, but risks abstraction; ground it further in physical detail or reaction.
Every time the prose stacks a named emotion or diagnosis after a strong image, it drops the score. Trust the scene's restraint.

drag_sections.location: He had not expected the chairs to bother him, and they bothered him.
drag_sections.why: Voss's emotional state is asserted rather than embodied; the prose tells us he is bothered but does not show it through action or dialogue.
drag_sections.fix: Show Voss's discomfort through a physical tic, hesitation, or a shift in his attention, rather than stating it outright.

drag_sections.location: "You set these out yourself," Voss said.
drag_sections.why: Dialogue here is functional but leans toward exposition, setting up the scene rather than revealing character through subtext or tension.
drag_sections.fix: Infuse the exchange with more subtext or indirectness, letting the arrangement of the chairs speak for itself through the characters' reactions.

drag_sections.location: He had the name in his hand, the way you have a coin in your hand, smooth and known and the right weight.
